elowen.bio: Elowen Vey grew up among the copyists of a lakeside library, where silence was a virtue and curiosity a vice. Childhood taught her that the careful ones are the ones who come home. She read every treatise on enchanted metal on its shelves until her tutors ran out of answers. On the road she turns back early rather than late, which is exactly why she is still on it. She came south to see arcane metal worked by hand instead of described in margins. When she first set out, she hoped to read the one book no library would lend. She fills the margins of every book she touches, including other people's. What came after she reached the village is the village's story to tell, not this one.

garrick.bio: Garrick Stone was raised by his mother Martha after his father died, and grew up carrying her firewood and her worries. He learned prayers before letters and has never quite stopped saying them. He swore his oath at a wayside shrine and spent two winters guarding pilgrims on the mountain roads. On the road he keeps the old wards and rites, and swears they have saved more lives than steel. He became a paladin to stand between ordinary people and the things that hunt them. When he first set out, he hoped to stand wherever the danger was worst. He mends his own gear and anyone else's who asks. Whatever he has done since arriving belongs to the village's own memory.

kestra.bio: Kestra Dunmore grew up with her brother Tobin in the crowded lanes of a river town, where wit was cheaper than bread. She learned early that nothing is truly lost until someone else has found it. She learned locks and quick exits from the very people she later came to owe money. In a tight corner she still finds a moment to check what the enemy was carrying. She took to adventuring because honest wages would never clear what she owes. When she first set out, she hoped for one great score and a quiet life after it. She never sits with her back to a door. Whatever she has done since arriving belongs to the village's own memory.

rv_aldous.bio: Aldous Brack was raised in a garrison town where pay day was the only holiday anyone kept. Long, plain days taught him to keep going when others stop. He sold his sword to merchant houses for twenty years and learned to read a contract faster than a map. In a tight corner he keeps a level head and a level blade. He now prefers small, well-paid work to grand causes, and keeps his own accounts. When he first set out, he hoped to earn a captain's trust and a captain's pay. He oils every blade at dusk, borrowed or not. Whatever he has done since arriving belongs to the village's own memory.

rv_dagny.bio: Dagny Ironvein was raised in a dwarven hall beneath the mountains, where oaths were carved into the doorposts. She learned early that nothing is truly lost until someone else has found it. She kept the old oaths as a hall-warden for longer than most of her companions have been alive. tomas.bio: Brother Tomas grew up in a busy market town, raised by a dice-maker who taught him the odds before his prayers. He learned prayers before letters and has never quite stopped saying them. He found his calling in a temple infirmary, where his jokes worked nearly as well as his poultices. In a tight corner he prays aloud, and fights no worse for it. He took to the road as a travelling healer, and the road's card tables took to him. When he first set out, he hoped to bring every companion home alive. He carries more bandages than coin. What came after he reached the village is the village's story to tell, not this one.

varn.bio: Varn Ashfang grew up among the hill clans, where a loud voice and an open hand were counted as wealth. He learned early that the quickest way through trouble is straight through the middle of it. He learned the great axe splitting firewood for a whole winter camp, and broke a good many handles doing it. On the road he strikes first and bandages later, and his scars keep count. He came down from the hills when the old songs stopped being enough for him. When he first set out, he hoped for a fight worth retelling by the fire. He laughs loudest when the odds are worst. Whatever he has done since arriving belongs to the village's own memory.

history.title: Hatchets and bucklers for the drovers' road
history.why: They write because 20 pieces have left your anvil and the village holds you in high renown.

offers.text: The Highmarsh Watch is doubling its patrols on the causeway. Captain Rourke wants forty iron shortswords and twenty round shields — and a captain's longsword for herself, worthy of the post.
offers.title: Forty blades and twenty round shields for the Highmarsh Watch
offers.why: They write because you delivered 1 major order well and your name is renowned.
